Course Title: Competitive Programming and Efficient Coding For Problem Solving
prerequisites: CSPC-100, CSPC-201 (Data Structures, Design and Analysis of Algorithms)
description: Identifying multiple alternate coding solutions of problems discussed in programming tests and competitive problems (CP) and developing understanding of their efficiency issues. Designing and developing brute-force solutions followed by time/space efficient solutions for CP problems. Learning commonly used problem solving approaches and applying them for coding solutions to new problems.

syllabus.title: Overview of Efficient Coding for Problem Solving and CP
syllabus.body: Introduction to competitive programming; revisit of complexity analysis; introduction to online platforms such as CodeChef, Codeforces and online submission; constraints during CP, online testing process and common errors such as TLE; use of STL.

syllabus.title: Use of Number Theory for Problem-Solving
syllabus.body: Reducing time/space complexity of brute force coding solution of Sieve Method, Inverse Module, Euclidean Method of factorization; efficient coding for Permutation Combination; XORing based and pattern-based solutions.

syllabus.title: Coding for Optimizing Time and Space using Sequential Storage
syllabus.body: Two pointer approach; problem-solving using arrays and strings such as rotation on sorted arrays, duplicate removal, string matching algorithms; Kadane's algorithm, stacks, priority-queues and hashing based efficient coding; median based problems and alternate solutions.

syllabus.title: Applying Non-Linear Data Structures for Real-life Problems
syllabus.body: Design of efficient solutions for problems such as finding loops in a linked list, memory efficient DLL, block reversal in LL; problem solving using trees and binary trees, Catalan numbers, applications of graphs, spanning tree and path algorithms for CP problems with reduced time/space complexity.

syllabus.title: CP Problem Solving using Advanced Topics
syllabus.body: Concept of disjoint sets and their efficient representation, algorithmic approaches such as Greedy, Backtracking, Dynamic Programming and applying them for CP problems using bottom-up dynamic programming.

outcomes: Understanding the issues of online platforms and Competitive Programming (CP) and developing brute force coding for commonly asked CP problems.
Analyzing the space and time complexity of brute force solutions and designing efficient solutions.
Evaluating the applicability of suitable algorithmic approaches to solve relevant CP problems.
Creating efficient solutions of CP problems using the learnt algorithmic approaches.
textbooks: Karumanchi, Data Structures and Algorithms Made Easy, CareerMonk Publications, 2017.
G L McDowell, Cracking the Coding Interviews, CareerCup Publications, 2016.
